source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság - Közbeszerzési Értesítő
why_relevant: Official gazette of Hungarian public procurement. Search results already surfaced concrete kiosk/automat notices (e.g. a municipal parking company procuring 133 new parking automats plus refurbishment of 83 ticket-issuing automats). Complements EKR with the published notice text and contract modifications.

source_name: BKK Budapesti Közlekedési Központ - hírek (jegy- és bérletautomata tenderek)
why_relevant: BKK publicly announces its ticket/pass vending machine tenders, network size and operator changes. Confirmed items: 2021 operations tender; Oct 2024 procurement to renew and expand the ~361-machine network; Mar 2025 note that refurbished and new machines may follow. This is the single richest narrative source on Budapest unattended payment estate.

source_name: MÁV-csoport hírek / MÁV-csoport magazin (jegykiadó automaták, MÁV-START + Volánbusz)
why_relevant: MÁV-VOLÁN group publishes rollout detail for shared ticket vending machines: e.g. 110 new machines (~HUF 1.1bn) split 93 Volánbusz / 11 HÉV / 6 MÁV-START, of which 30 are card-only and the rest accept cash and card. Directly quantifies unattended payment demand and acceptance mix outside banking.

source_name: MÁV-csoport üvegzseb / szerződések közzététele
why_relevant: Hungarian 'üvegzseb' (glass-pocket) transparency rules force state companies to publish contracts above a threshold, including supplier name and value. A historic contract list PDF was found on mavcsoport.hu, indicating the disclosure channel exists for rail/bus ticketing and terminal contracts.

source_name: MNV Zrt. Szerződéskereső (state asset manager contract search)
why_relevant: Searchable contract database of the Hungarian National Asset Management company, the owner of many partly state-owned buyers in this cell. Useful for tracing supplier relationships that never reach the press.

source_name: Kozadat.hu közadatkereső (public data / institution registry)
why_relevant: Aggregator that maps Hungarian public institutions to their statutory disclosure pages, including contract registers. Good snowballing entry point to find the disclosure URL of hospitals, transport operators and utilities in this cell.

source_name: KiMitTud (FOI request platform, Hungary)
why_relevant: Public archive of freedom-of-information requests and the answers given by Hungarian public bodies. A legitimate route to obtain machine counts, supplier names and maintenance contracts for hospitals, transport operators and state companies that do not publish them.

source_name: NAV eNYUGTA - forgalmazási engedélyek (approved e-cash-register types and distributors)
why_relevant: The tax authority's authoritative register of licensed (e-)cash-register types and their distributors. Hungary's shift to e-pénztárgép (hardware licence numbers starting with B, cloud ones with C) reshapes the whole POS/SCO hardware field: the licence list effectively enumerates who can legally sell checkout hardware/software to retail, fuel and hospitality buyers.

source_name: BFKH / MKEH mérésügy - pénztárgép hatósági oldal
why_relevant: Metrology/licensing authority pages for cash registers and taximeters - the technical approval side of payment-accepting devices, including type approvals and technical requirements relevant to unattended and self-checkout hardware.

source_name: Trade magazin (FMCG/retail trade press)
why_relevant: The leading Hungarian FMCG/retail trade magazine, with a dedicated self-checkout tag and coverage of chain-by-chain rollouts, voucher acceptance issues at SCO, and OKSZ positions. Frequently names technology suppliers and quantifies installed base.

source_name: OKSZ - Országos Kereskedelmi Szövetség
why_relevant: Retail industry association whose members are the large chains (Tesco, SPAR, Lidl, Auchan, Aldi and Hungarian-owned retailers). Publishes positions on self-checkout, cash handling and payment acceptance obligations, and is a reliable pointer to which chains are affected by new checkout legislation.

source_name: SPAR Magyarország sajtószoba
why_relevant: Retailer's own press room; confirmed to publish self-checkout rollout announcements including share of transactions handled at SCO. Directly evidences non-bank self-service demand and, occasionally, the technology partner.

source_name: Economx / Világgazdaság / Index business desks - retail self-checkout and procurement reporting
why_relevant: Hungarian business media reliably publish the numbers that companies do not: installed self-checkout counts per chain (e.g. Tesco ~1028, SPAR ~900, Lidl ~1300 units reported in 2025), and procurement outcomes such as the operator change of the BKK vending network. Best single channel for quantified installed base and contract-award colour.

source_name: Szintézis Informatikai Zrt. - self-checkout / retail systems integrator
why_relevant: Hungarian IT integrator that publicly documents NCR-based self-checkout deployments in Hungarian stores (reference: a Príma store in Budaörs). Integrator reference pages reveal the vendor-to-buyer chain that procurement notices often hide behind a reseller name.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (Hungary) - company filings and profile aggregators
why_relevant: Hungarian company registry aggregators (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN, iCégtár, Kompass) expose revenue, headcount, ownership and even won-tender lists for local subsidiaries of self-service hardware vendors. Lets the competitive field for SCO/ATM/kiosk in HU be sized from filings rather than press claims; the same method applies to NCR Voyix, Toshiba GCS, Laurel and local integrators.

source_name: Laurel Zrt. / LAURA-SSC - domestic self-checkout developer
why_relevant: A Hungarian-developed self-checkout line (LAURA-SSC, RFID-based, referenced at Decathlon and reported as deployed in Hungary plus several other countries), positioned as a low-cost alternative to international systems. A domestic competitor that banking-only searching would never surface.

source_name: Banktech Kft. - kiosk / self-service terminal vendor (HU)
why_relevant: Hungarian vendor page dedicated to self-service kiosk terminals, i.e. a direct competitor/partner in the unattended segment serving both bank and non-bank buyers (retail, fuel, hospitality, public services).

source_name: FOXPOST / Packeta Hungary - parcel locker network communications
why_relevant: Post-merger (completed 2026) the combined FOXPOST-Packeta network is reported at roughly 3,800 parcel lockers plus ~1,350 pickup points (>5,000 collection points). Their card-acceptance model changes are a leading indicator for unattended payment hardware demand: card payment at the machine is being narrowed to non-registered senders while pre-payment shifts to SimplePay online.

source_name: Budapest Főváros / budapest.hu + Budapesti Közlekedési szakportálok - parking automat policy
why_relevant: The municipality announced that from 1 July 2026 Budapest parking goes cashless and thousands of parking automats are removed, with the cost of maintaining them and repeated scandal-hit parking-automat procurement tenders cited as reasons. A structural, negative demand signal for one whole unattended-payment segment, and a pointer to the historic district-level procurement record.

source_name: openprocurements.com Hungary - CPV-indexed procurement browser
why_relevant: Third-party index of Hungarian procurement notices organised by CPV code (e.g. 51214000 parking-meter installation services). Useful for discovering the right CPV codes for kiosks, ticket machines, POS terminals and cash-handling equipment, which then makes EKR/TED searching far more complete.

source_name: magyarvasut.hu / iho.hu - rail and transport specialist press
why_relevant: Specialist Hungarian transport trade media that cover ticketing digitalisation in operational detail (EGY JEGY unified ticketing programme, vending-machine expansion, payment acceptance types). Often earlier and more technical than mainstream press, and a strong pointer to supplier and integrator names.

source_name: MOL Nyrt. corporate site and station documentation
why_relevant: Hungary's largest fuel retailer and a major payment-acceptance estate (fuel cards, station POS, vignette kiosks/tablets, MOL Plugee self-service EV charging with app-based payment). Site documents (station lists, receipt/invoice rules, fuel-card terms) describe the acceptance environment even where no procurement notice exists, since MOL is a private buyer.

source_name: Store Insider (HU retail-tech portal)
why_relevant: Hungarian retail-technology portal publishing shopper-behaviour and store-technology data on self-checkout usage (e.g. three of four purchases going through self-checkout in surveyed contexts). Useful for demand-side sizing and for spotting new store-tech suppliers entering HU.

source_name: Pályázati Portál – Támogatott projektkereső (palyazat.gov.hu, supported-project search)
source_subtype: government grant-beneficiary register / searchable database with export
why_relevant: Central Hungarian register of every EU-cofinanced supported project (~529k records observed) with beneficiary name, project title, awarded amount, decision date, OP code and location; filterable by operative programme (GINOP/GINOP Plusz, DIMOP Plusz, KÖFOP) and applicant name, with an Export function. This is the primary way to enumerate funded digitalisation projects at banks, savings institutions, fintechs, payment/POS integrators and public financial IT bodies (Magyar Államkincstár, NAV) before or instead of a procurement notice.

source_name: Pályázati Portál – Pályázatkereső (open calls) and call documentation
why_relevant: Forward-looking pipeline: the call texts (felhívás) define eligible digitalisation activities, budget envelopes, eligible supplier/accreditation rules and deadlines. Reading DIMOP Plusz and GINOP Plusz calls tells you what demand is about to hit the market and which vendor categories are eligible for reimbursement.

source_name: Pályázati Portál – RRF (Helyreállítási és Ellenállóképességi Eszköz) section
source_subtype: national RRF programme page + call documents
why_relevant: Hungarian-side landing point for RRF components and calls; RRF has a large digitalisation share (reported ~29.8% of the plan) and funds public digital services with payment/identity components. Useful for tracing which RRF investment lines create demand for payment, identity and core-system integration work.

source_name: digitalismegujulas.kormany.hu – DIMOP Plusz managing-authority site and supported-project base data
why_relevant: Managing authority for the Digital Renewal OP Plus, the single most relevant OP for financial/payment IT. Publishes programme documents and supported-project base data (including the KÖFOP legacy list), which name beneficiary public bodies and project scope.

source_name: Vállalkozz digitálisan! / Modern Vállalkozások Programja – accredited supplier & product catalogue (MKIK)
source_subtype: accredited vendor/product catalogue tied to grant eligibility
why_relevant: Highest-value vendor source in this cell: DIMOP Plusz SME digitalisation calls (e.g. 1.2.6/B, 1.2.6/C) require purchases from this accredited supplier catalogue. Reported to list 1650+ IT suppliers and 3000+ digital products/services, each with a per-supplier page — an effectively complete, state-sanctioned map of who is allowed to sell subsidised digitalisation (including POS, e-invoicing, online payment and ERP-payment modules) in Hungary.
